summary: Iteration 11 — frontend-only end-to-end verification of the TWO new flagship interactions: (1) Card-Flip-on-Long-Press with CVV/Billing/Freeze on Dashboard + More; (2) Bloom Confetti on Retirement bonsai milestones. Seeded via POST /api/demo/seed → Jordan Taylor / elite / user id 6b03b11f-…. Gate keys set (milli_token, milli_selected_plan, milli_onboarding_complete, milli_splash_seen). issues: At the reveal-tilt (rotateX 6°, rotateZ -8°) the 3D-flipped back face renders slightly skewed and the 'Address on file' billing text overlaps visually with the FREEZE CARD pill button. Consider suppressing the tilt/skew when flipped=true so the back face reads flat and legible.

action_items: OPTIONAL: When card is flipped, set rotateZ/rotateX to 0 so the back face reads flat (currently the reveal-tilt is preserved and overlaps text at some viewport widths).

OPTIONAL: Persist billing address on the demo-seed user (currently falls back to literal 'Address on file' string because Jordan has no address_line1/city). Add city/state/zip to demo seed for a richer back-face demo.
critical_code_review_comments: MilliCard.jsx cancelHold() short-tap flip-back logic uses Date.now()-holdStart.current < 400 AFTER the setTimeout for long-press has ALREADY fired. This works because startHold sets holdStart at the beginning and the 500ms hold that flipped it to back is > 400 ms, so the short-tap-back branch is skipped correctly on the flip-triggering release. However if a user long-presses the FRONT and holds >400ms then releases, the short-tap branch will not fire (correct), but if a user long-presses on the BACK (holds 500ms while back is visible), the setTimeout will re-flip to front AND then the cancelHold guard `flipped && …<400` will be false (400ms elapsed), so no double-flip. Logic is sound but subtle — worth a code comment.

MilliCard.jsx: freeze toggle attempts to POST /card/freeze via dynamic import of @/lib/api. Verified backend logs no such endpoint exists yet; currently swallowed via console.debug. Fine for now but flag for a future endpoint or remove the placeholder.

BloomPetals.jsx uses inline <style>{`@keyframes mv-petal…`}</style> inside a React component — every mount re-injects the keyframes into the head. Not a leak (React de-dupes on unmount), but consider hoisting to a CSS file for perf.

Retirement.jsx petals useEffect depends only on bonsaiProgress and user.id — since bonsaiProgress is only set once on mount (no polling), petals only ever fire on initial load after a milestone was crossed elsewhere. If future backend adds live vault updates, add polling or WS listener so the celebration fires the moment a user hits 25/50/75/100 % in-session.
